questions.question_en: If two distinct non-zero real variables x and y are such that (x + y) is proportional to (x − y), then the value of x / y:
questions.question_hi:
[Algebraic Proportions • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
If two distinct non-zero real variables x and y are such that (x + y) is proportional to (x − y), then the value of x / y:
options_en: depends only on x and not on y
depends only on y and not on x
options_hi: depends only on x and not on y
depends only on y and not on x
questions.explanation_en: Given (x + y) = k(x − y) for a constant k ≠ ±1 (since x, y are distinct and non-zero). Rearranging gives x(k − 1) = y(k + 1) => x / y = (k + 1) / (k − 1), which is a constant.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
Given (x + y) = k(x − y) for a constant k ≠ ±1 (since x, y are distinct and non-zero). Rearranging gives x(k − 1) = y(k + 1) => x / y = (k + 1) / (k − 1), which is a constant.

questions.question_en: The number of coins of Rs. 1, Rs. 5, and Rs. 10 denominations that a person has are in the ratio 5 : 3 : 13. Of the total amount, the percentage of money in Rs. 5 coins is:

questions.question_en: For positive non-zero real variables p and q, if log(p² + q²) = log p + log q + 2 log 3, then the value of (p⁴ + q⁴) / (p² q²) is:
questions.question_hi:
[Logarithmic Identities • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
For positive non-zero real variables p and q, if log(p² + q²) = log p + log q + 2 log 3, then the value of (p⁴ + q⁴) / (p² q²) is:
questions.explanation_en: From log(p² + q²) = log(9pq), we have p² + q² = 9pq, so (p² + q²)/(pq) = 9. Squaring both sides: (p⁴ + 2p²q² + q⁴)/(p²q²) = 81 => (p⁴ + q⁴)/(p²q²) = 81 − 2 = 79.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
From log(p² + q²) = log(9pq), we have p² + q² = 9pq, so (p² + q²)/(pq) = 9. Squaring both sides: (p⁴ + 2p²q² + q⁴)/(p²q²) = 81 => (p⁴ + q⁴)/(p²q²) = 81 − 2 = 79.

questions.question_en: Five persons P, Q, R, S, and T are sitting in a row not necessarily in the same order. Q and R are separated by one person, and S is not seated adjacent to Q. How many distinct seating arrangements are possible if P and T occupy the two extreme ends?
questions.question_hi:
[Permutations & Seating • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Five persons P, Q, R, S, and T are sitting in a row not necessarily in the same order. Q and R are separated by one person, and S is not seated adjacent to Q. How many distinct seating arrangements are possible if P and T occupy the two extreme ends?
questions.explanation_en: The two ends (positions 1 and 5) are occupied by P and T in 2! = 2 ways. The middle three positions (2, 3, 4) are occupied by Q, R, S. Since Q and R have one person between them, Q and R must occupy positions (2, 4) in 2! = 2 ways, forcing S into position 3 (which would be adjacent to Q). Wait—if P or T is between Q and R, then only 4 valid arrangements exist where S is at an end. With P and T fixed at ends, there are 2 × 2 = 4 arrangements of {Q, R} at (2,4).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
The two ends (positions 1 and 5) are occupied by P and T in 2! = 2 ways. The middle three positions (2, 3, 4) are occupied by Q, R, S. Since Q and R have one person between them, Q and R must occupy positions (2, 4) in 2! = 2 ways, forcing S into position 3 (which would be adjacent to Q). Wait—if P or T is between Q and R, then only 4 valid arrangements exist where S is at an end. With P and T fixed at ends, there are 2 × 2 = 4 arrangements of {Q, R} at (2,4).

questions.question_en: Two identical rectangular sheets A and B of dimensions 24 cm × 16 cm are folded twice: Sheet A is folded twice along its longer side to form a 6 cm × 16 cm rectangle, whereas Sheet B is folded twice along its shorter side to form a 24 cm × 4 cm rectangle. The ratio of the perimeter of folded Sheet B to folded Sheet A is:
questions.question_hi:
[Geometry & Perimeter Folding • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Two identical rectangular sheets A and B of dimensions 24 cm × 16 cm are folded twice: Sheet A is folded twice along its longer side to form a 6 cm × 16 cm rectangle, whereas Sheet B is folded twice along its shorter side to form a 24 cm × 4 cm rectangle. The ratio of the perimeter of folded Sheet B to folded Sheet A is:
questions.explanation_en: Perimeter of folded Sheet A (6 cm × 16 cm) = 2 × (6 + 16) = 44 cm. Perimeter of folded Sheet B (24 cm × 4 cm) = 2 × (24 + 4) = 56 cm. Ratio of B to A = 56 : 44 = 14 : 11.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
Perimeter of folded Sheet A (6 cm × 16 cm) = 2 × (6 + 16) = 44 cm. Perimeter of folded Sheet B (24 cm × 4 cm) = 2 × (24 + 4) = 56 cm. Ratio of B to A = 56 : 44 = 14 : 11.

questions.question_en: The first-order differential equation M(x, y) dx + N(x, y) dy = 0 on a simply connected domain in R² is exact if and only if:

questions.question_en:
Let R[X², X³] be the subring of the polynomial ring R[X] generated by X² and X³. Consider the statements:
(I) The ideal ⟨X², X³⟩ in R[X², X³] is a principal ideal.
(II) R[X², X³] is a Unique Factorization Domain (UFD).
Which one of the following is correct?
questions.question_hi:
[Abstract Algebra (Ring Theory) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let R[X², X³] be the subring of the polynomial ring R[X] generated by X² and X³. Consider the statements:
(I) The ideal ⟨X², X³⟩ in R[X², X³] is a principal ideal.
(II) R[X², X³] is a Unique Factorization Domain (UFD).
Which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation_en: In R[X², X³] (polynomially lacking the linear term X), X² and X³ are both irreducible, and (X²)³ = X⁶ = (X³)² gives two distinct factorizations into irreducibles, so R[X², X³] is NOT a UFD and ⟨X², X³⟩ is not principal. Both (I) and (II) are FALSE.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
In R[X², X³] (polynomially lacking the linear term X), X² and X³ are both irreducible, and (X²)³ = X⁶ = (X³)² gives two distinct factorizations into irreducibles, so R[X², X³] is NOT a UFD and ⟨X², X³⟩ is not principal. Both (I) and (II) are FALSE.

questions.question_en: Consider the topology on the set of integers Z generated by the basis {S(a, b) : a, b ∈ Z, a ≠ 0}, where S(a, b) = {a n + b : n ∈ Z} is a bi-infinite arithmetic progression. In this topology, every basis set S(a, b) is:
questions.question_hi:
[Topology on Z (Furstenberg Topology) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Consider the topology on the set of integers Z generated by the basis {S(a, b) : a, b ∈ Z, a ≠ 0}, where S(a, b) = {a n + b : n ∈ Z} is a bi-infinite arithmetic progression. In this topology, every basis set S(a, b) is:
questions.explanation_en: Each arithmetic progression S(a, b) is open by definition of basis. Its complement in Z is the union of the finitely many other residue classes mod |a|, each of which is open. Hence S(a, b) is also closed (clopen).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
Each arithmetic progression S(a, b) is open by definition of basis. Its complement in Z is the union of the finitely many other residue classes mod |a|, each of which is open. Hence S(a, b) is also closed (clopen).

questions.question_en: Let A = [[0, 2], [2, 0]] and let T : M2(C) → M2(C) be the linear operator defined by T(B) = AB. The trace and determinant of the linear operator T are, respectively:
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Linear Transformations on Matrices) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let A = [[0, 2], [2, 0]] and let T : M2(C) → M2(C) be the linear operator defined by T(B) = AB. The trace and determinant of the linear operator T are, respectively:
questions.explanation_en: The eigenvalues of A = [[0, 2], [2, 0]] are λ1 = 2 and λ2 = −2. Since T(B) = AB acts on the two columns of B independently as A ⊕ A, the eigenvalues of T are {2, 2, −2, −2}. Thus Trace(T) = 2 + 2 − 2 − 2 = 0 and det(T) = (2)(2)(−2)(−2) = 16.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
The eigenvalues of A = [[0, 2], [2, 0]] are λ1 = 2 and λ2 = −2. Since T(B) = AB acts on the two columns of B independently as A ⊕ A, the eigenvalues of T are {2, 2, −2, −2}. Thus Trace(T) = 2 + 2 − 2 − 2 = 0 and det(T) = (2)(2)(−2)(−2) = 16.

questions.question_en: Let y1(x) and y2(x) be two linearly independent solutions of the homogeneous second-order ODE y'' + P(x)y' + Q(x)y = 0 on [a, b], where P, Q are continuous. Which statement about their Wronskian W(y1, y2)(x) is always TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[ODE & Wronskian Theory • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let y1(x) and y2(x) be two linearly independent solutions of the homogeneous second-order ODE y'' + P(x)y' + Q(x)y = 0 on [a, b], where P, Q are continuous. Which statement about their Wronskian W(y1, y2)(x) is always TRUE?
options_en: W(x) vanishes at exactly one point in (a, b)
W(x) is never zero on [a, b]
W(x) is a non-zero constant only when Q(x) = 0
options_hi: W(x) vanishes at exactly one point in (a, b)
W(x) is never zero on [a, b]
W(x) is a non-zero constant only when Q(x) = 0
questions.explanation_en: By Abel's identity, W(x) = W(x0) exp(−∫ P(t) dt). Since y1 and y2 are linearly independent solutions on [a, b], W(x0) ≠ 0, so W(x) is never zero on [a, b].
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
By Abel's identity, W(x) = W(x0) exp(−∫ P(t) dt). Since y1 and y2 are linearly independent solutions on [a, b], W(x0) ≠ 0, so W(x) is never zero on [a, b].

questions.question_en: Let A ∈ M_n(C) be a normal matrix (i.e., A A* = A* A). Which of the following statement(s) is/are always TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Normal Matrices) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let A ∈ M_n(C) be a normal matrix (i.e., A A* = A* A). Which of the following statement(s) is/are always TRUE?
options_en: A is unitarily diagonalizable over C.
If all eigenvalues of A are real, then A is Hermitian.
If all eigenvalues of A have absolute value 1, then A is unitary.
A must be a real symmetric matrix.
options_hi: A is unitarily diagonalizable over C.
If all eigenvalues of A are real, then A is Hermitian.
If all eigenvalues of A have absolute value 1, then A is unitary.
A must be a real symmetric matrix.
questions.explanation_en: By the Spectral Theorem over C, a matrix A is normal iff A = U D U* for a unitary matrix U and diagonal matrix D of eigenvalues. If D is real, A* = U D U* = A (Hermitian); if |λ_i| = 1, D D* = I so A A* = I (unitary).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
By the Spectral Theorem over C, a matrix A is normal iff A = U D U* for a unitary matrix U and diagonal matrix D of eigenvalues. If D is real, A* = U D U* = A (Hermitian); if |λ_i| = 1, D D* = I so A A* = I (unitary).

questions.question_en: Let f : (0, 1) → R be a continuous function. Which of the following condition(s) guarantee(s) that f is uniformly continuous on (0, 1)?
questions.question_hi:
[Real Analysis (Uniform Continuity & Compactness) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let f : (0, 1) → R be a continuous function. Which of the following condition(s) guarantee(s) that f is uniformly continuous on (0, 1)?
options_en: Both limits lim_{x→0+} f(x) and lim_{x→1−} f(x) exist finitely in R.
f has a bounded derivative f'(x) on (0, 1).
options_hi: Both limits lim_{x→0+} f(x) and lim_{x→1−} f(x) exist finitely in R.
f has a bounded derivative f'(x) on (0, 1).
questions.explanation_en: A continuous function on a bounded open interval (0, 1) is uniformly continuous iff it can be extended continuously to [0, 1] (i.e., finite limits exist at 0+ and 1−). Also, a bounded derivative |f'(x)| ≤ M implies f is Lipschitz by the Mean Value Theorem, hence uniformly continuous. Mere boundedness (e.g., sin(1/x)) is insufficient.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
A continuous function on a bounded open interval (0, 1) is uniformly continuous iff it can be extended continuously to [0, 1] (i.e., finite limits exist at 0+ and 1−). Also, a bounded derivative |f'(x)| ≤ M implies f is Lipschitz by the Mean Value Theorem, hence uniformly continuous. Mere boundedness (e.g., sin(1/x)) is insufficient.

Let X = {(x, y) ∈ R² : x² + y² = 1} be the unit circle equipped with the subspace topology from R². Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

Every continuous real-valued function on X attains its supremum and infimum.
X is homeomorphic to the closed interval [0, 1].
questions.explanation_en: The unit circle S¹ is closed and bounded in R², hence compact by Heine-Borel, so any continuous f : S¹ → R attains its extreme values. Removing any single point p leaves S¹ \ {p} homeomorphic to (0, 1), which is connected (making S¹ not homeomorphic to [0, 1]).
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
The unit circle S¹ is closed and bounded in R², hence compact by Heine-Borel, so any continuous f : S¹ → R attains its extreme values. Removing any single point p leaves S¹ \ {p} homeomorphic to (0, 1), which is connected (making S¹ not homeomorphic to [0, 1]).

questions.question_en: The total number of group homomorphisms from the cyclic group Z/4Z into the symmetric group S4 is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Group Theory (Group Homomorphisms) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The total number of group homomorphisms from the cyclic group Z/4Z into the symmetric group S4 is ________.
questions.explanation_en: A homomorphism φ : Z/4Z → S4 is determined by φ(1), which can be any element in S4 whose order divides 4 (i.e., order 1, 2, or 4). In S4, there is 1 identity (order 1), 6 transpositions (order 2), 3 double transpositions (order 2), and 6 four-cycles (order 4). Total = 1 + 6 + 3 + 6 = 16.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):
A homomorphism φ : Z/4Z → S4 is determined by φ(1), which can be any element in S4 whose order divides 4 (i.e., order 1, 2, or 4). In S4, there is 1 identity (order 1), 6 transpositions (order 2), 3 double transpositions (order 2), and 6 four-cycles (order 4). Total = 1 + 6 + 3 + 6 = 16.

questions.question_en: If the outward flux of the vector field F(x, y, z) = (x³, y³, z³) across the unit sphere x² + y² + z² = 1 is (k π) / 5, then the value of k is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Vector Calculus (Divergence Theorem) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
If the outward flux of the vector field F(x, y, z) = (x³, y³, z³) across the unit sphere x² + y² + z² = 1 is (k π) / 5, then the value of k is ________.
questions.explanation_en: By Gauss's Divergence Theorem, Flux = ∭_B div(F) dV = ∭_B 3(x² + y² + z²) dV. In spherical coordinates over r ∈ [0, 1]: Flux = 3 × (4π) ∫_0^1 r² · r² dr = 12π × (1/5) = 12π/5. Hence k = 12.

आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):

questions.question_en: Consider the Linear Programming Problem (LPP): Minimize Z = 5 x1 + 2 x2 subject to x1 + x2 ≥ 4, x1 + 2 x2 ≥ 4, and x1, x2 ≥ 0. The minimum value of Z is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Programming (Extreme Point Optimization) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Consider the Linear Programming Problem (LPP): Minimize Z = 5 x1 + 2 x2 subject to x1 + x2 ≥ 4, x1 + 2 x2 ≥ 4, and x1, x2 ≥ 0. The minimum value of Z is ________.
questions.explanation_en: The corner points of the unbounded feasible region in the first quadrant are (4, 0) where Z = 20, and (0, 4) where both constraints hold (0+4 ≥ 4 and 0+8 ≥ 4) giving Z = 5(0) + 2(4) = 8. Thus Z_min = 8.

questions.question_en: Let f(x, y, z) = x² y + y² z + z² x. The magnitude of the gradient vector ∇f at the point (1, 1, 1) is √N. The value of N is ________.
questions.question_hi:

Let f(x, y, z) = x² y + y² z + z² x. The magnitude of the gradient vector ∇f at the point (1, 1, 1) is √N. The value of N is ________.

questions.question_en: Let C be the positively oriented circle |z| = 3 in the complex plane. If ∮_C [(z² + 1) / (z(z − 2))] dz = 2πi × K, then the real number K is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Complex Analysis (Cauchy Residue Theorem) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let C be the positively oriented circle |z| = 3 in the complex plane. If ∮_C [(z² + 1) / (z(z − 2))] dz = 2πi × K, then the real number K is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Inside |z| = 3, g(z) = (z² + 1)/(z(z − 2)) has simple poles at z = 0 and z = 2. Res(g, 0) = 1/(−2) = −0.5 and Res(g, 2) = (4 + 1)/2 = 2.5. By Cauchy's Residue Theorem, K = −0.5 + 2.5 = 2.0.

आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024):

questions.question_en: Using Simpson's 1/3 rule with step size h = 1 on the interval [0, 2], the numerical approximation to ∫_0^2 (3x² + 2x + 1) dx is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Numerical Analysis (Trapezoidal & Simpson Rule) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Using Simpson's 1/3 rule with step size h = 1 on the interval [0, 2], the numerical approximation to ∫_0^2 (3x² + 2x + 1) dx is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Since Simpson's 1/3 rule is exact for polynomials of degree ≤ 3, it gives the exact integral: [x³ + x² + x]_0^2 = 8 + 4 + 2 = 14.

questions.question_en: Let W be the subspace of R⁵ spanned by the vectors v1 = (1, 2, 0, −1, 3), v2 = (0, 1, 1, 2, −1), and v3 = (1, 3, 1, 1, 2). The dimension of the orthogonal complement W^⊥ in R⁵ is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Linear Algebra (Dimension of Orthogonal Complement) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
Let W be the subspace of R⁵ spanned by the vectors v1 = (1, 2, 0, −1, 3), v2 = (0, 1, 1, 2, −1), and v3 = (1, 3, 1, 1, 2). The dimension of the orthogonal complement W^⊥ in R⁵ is ________.
questions.explanation_en: Notice that v3 = v1 + v2, while v1 and v2 are linearly independent. Thus dim(W) = 2, and by the rank-nullity / orthogonal decomposition theorem in R⁵, dim(W^⊥) = 5 − dim(W) = 5 − 2 = 3.

questions.question_en: In a group G of order 45, the sum of the number of Sylow 3-subgroups and the number of Sylow 5-subgroups is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Abstract Algebra (Sylow Subgroups) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
In a group G of order 45, the sum of the number of Sylow 3-subgroups and the number of Sylow 5-subgroups is ________.
questions.explanation_en: |G| = 45 = 3² × 5. By Sylow's Third Theorem, n3 ≡ 1 (mod 3) and n3 | 5 => n3 = 1; similarly n5 ≡ 1 (mod 5) and n5 | 9 => n5 = 1. Thus n3 + n5 = 1 + 1 = 2.
questions.explanation_hi:

questions.question_en: The smallest positive eigenvalue λ of the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem y'' + λ y = 0 on [0, π] with boundary conditions y'(0) = 0 and y(π) = 0 is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Ordinary Differential Equations (Boundary Value Problem) • GATE Mathematics (MA) • Feb 2024]
The smallest positive eigenvalue λ of the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem y'' + λ y = 0 on [0, π] with boundary conditions y'(0) = 0 and y(π) = 0 is ________.
questions.explanation_en: For λ = k² > 0, y(x) = A cos(kx) + B sin(kx). y'(0) = 0 implies B = 0. Then y(π) = A cos(kπ) = 0 requires kπ = (2n − 1)π/2 => k_min = 1/2, so λ_min = k_min² = (1/2)² = 0.25.
